space-bunny-free.reason: X is the longer, quote-dense script: nearly every number is attributed, it builds a real fire-department-to-harness through-line, and it hands builders six concrete habits from Anthropic's prompting guide, but it rides on a long tail of newsletter specifics it cannot cross-check and its Build Pitch breaks frame by pointing at Kyle's private pitch folder and asking him to greenlight a build. Y is the tighter and more disciplined script: it names its gaps up front (unlabelled Moonshots transcript, summary-only items), discloses Dave Blundin's conflict of interest, corrects its own source's arithmetic, and keeps the pitch purely general, at the cost of leaving the a16z, Willison, MIT Tech Review and Nvidia beats as one-line stubs.

opus.reason: X hedges carefully and marks every summary-only source, but it relies on several callbacks to earlier episodes ('we flagged on the nineteenth', 'Thursday's episode', 'the Noah Smith and Ramez Naam argument we covered yesterday') that can't be checked against today's material, and its build pitch is concrete, sourced and kept general. Y goes deeper, especially on the MIT liability piece and Anthropic's prompting guide, and ties its threads together well, but it pads the sports section with inference and unsourced background, and its build pitch breaks the privacy rule by naming Kyle, the build-pitches folder and the show's own AI pipeline and QC setup.
